jas: heads-up — my async sample harness started showing weird behavior under mid-level load: after a cluster of 429s the local TokenBucket sometimes increased tokens and allowed another burst.

nora: that sounds like the header-merge + async race. can you paste a captured 429 response?

jas: pasted one (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: -3
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712000000
X-Quota-Limit: 1500
X-Quota-Remaining: 5
X-Quota-Window: 60
Retry-After: 45000
Content-Type: application/json
```

raf ael: interesting — two issues here: negative remaining and mismatch between X-RateLimit and X-Quota. our client merge currently prefers whichever header is present (or last-write), which is unsafe. we should always pick the safe min when different counters refer to the same resource.

tina: agreed. obvious fixes: 1) canonicalize header keys to lower-case early. 2) clamp any remaining < 0 to 0 at parse time. 3) when both quota and ratelimit are present, derive remaining = min(quota_remaining, ratelimit_remaining). 4) Retry-After: prefer retry-after-ms when present (ms->seconds). otherwise parse retry-after as seconds but use a heuristic to catch ms mis-sends (if value > 10000 treat as ms and divide by 1000). document the threshold.

jas: i prototyped small pure helpers in the sample app to validate semantics (typed for mypy):
```py
from typing import Mapping, TypedDict

class RateLimits(TypedDict):
    limit: int
    remaining: int
    reset: int


def parse_retry_after(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> float:
    h = {k.lower(): v for k, v in headers.items()}
    if 'retry-after-ms' in h:
        try:
            return int(h['retry-after-ms']) / 1000.0
        except Exception:
            return 0.0
    if 'retry-after' in h:
        try:
            v = float(h['retry-after'])
        except Exception:
            return 0.0
        # heuristic: very large numbers likely ms mis-sent
        if v > 10000:
            return v / 1000.0
        return v
    return 0.0


def parse_rate_headers(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> RateLimits:
    h = {k.lower(): v for k, v in headers.items()}
    rl_limit = int(h.get('x-ratelimit-limit', '0'))
    rl_rem = max(0, int(h.get('x-ratelimit-remaining', '0')))
    quota_limit = int(h.get('x-quota-limit', '0'))
    quota_rem = max(0, int(h.get('x-quota-remaining', '0')))
    # if both present, take safe min of remaining and prefer explicit reset/window fields
    remaining = min(x for x in (rl_rem, quota_rem) if x is not None)
    reset = int(h.get('x-ratelimit-reset', h.get('x-quota-window', '0')))
    limit = rl_limit or quota_limit
    return RateLimits(limit=limit, remaining=remaining, reset=reset)
```

nora: small nit: don't use min(x for x in ...) — that comprehension will error if one is 0. simpler: remaining = min(rl_rem, quota_rem) if rl_rem and quota_rem else rl_rem or quota_rem. also add robust int parsing with fallback to 0 for malformed values.

rafael: on the async side we must make TokenBucket.update_from_headers atomic. propose AsyncTokenBucket with an internal asyncio.Lock and async def update_from_headers(headers). Sync TokenBucket reuses the pure parse helpers so both code paths have identical semantics. add a fast integration test that spins up an aiohttp mock server and returns deterministic header sequences to exercise races.

tina: yes. add unit tests for: mixed-case header names, negative remaining clamped to 0, ms vs seconds heuristics (including malformed values), and the concurrency repro. include a --dev flag to log raw headers for triage so we can enable it in customer reproductions.

jas: opened draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py-sdk/pull/2615 with parse helpers, clamping, safe-merge logic, AsyncTokenBucket.update_from_headers (asyncio.Lock), unit tests, and a small concurrency repro. CI pending.

ci-bot: PR 2615 opened by jas — CI queued :github: 

rafael: i'll review the PR today. if it lands we'll add a short entry to the SDK changelog and a docs note explaining the Retry-After heuristic and why we choose the safe-min merge.

tina: thanks everyone. once merged i'll add a tiny sample-app README that reproduces the issue so integrators can validate their gateways. :thumbsup:
